title: Fraction, Decimal, Percent: Same Number, Different Costume
preview: 1/2 = 0.5 = 50% — three costumes for the same number. Walk past the easy cases into repeating decimals, percents > 100%, percents < 1%, and the decimal-shift trap.

body.goal: Students see that fractions, decimals, and percents are interchangeable representations of the same value — and don't break when the value is repeating, greater than 1, or less than 1%.
body.launch: Run the warm-up so the equivalent-fraction and ÷100 moves are warm. Then start the slice. The diamond is in steps 7-12 — let groups argue.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up the moves you'll use: equivalent fractions and multiplying/dividing by 100.

prerequisiteSteps.teacherNote: Tiny decimal, useful for the < 1% case later.

steps.teacherNote: Reverse direction — decimal back to fraction.
Compare to step 5 — same answer flipped.
Diamond: repeating decimal. What do you write? Some kids will round to 0.33.
Or 33⅓%. Push: is '33%' close enough, or actually wrong?
Diamond: decimal-shift trap. Multiply by 100 → 5%, NOT 0.05%.
Confirm the shift in reverse. Divide by 100 → 0.05.
Diamond: greater than 1. Many kids think 100% is the max.
Diamond: less than 1%. Many kids think percents are whole numbers.

enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Forces conversion to a common form before comparing. \frac{7}{12} = 0.583...
Terminates but isn't a 'nice' percent — challenges the pattern.
= 2/1, just 2. Push: where did the bar go?
Tiny percent territory. Decimal shift two places.

body.consolidation: Bring it back. 'Step 11 went over 100%. Step 12 went below 1%. Are those still legal? How do you know? Step 7 had a repeating decimal — was 0.3 enough, or did you need more? In enrichment 1, you had to convert all four to compare them. Which form was easiest to compare in?'
